svg.text: Why running this on Spyre took real work
The model was written for GPUs. Spyre is a different kind of machine, so the recipe had to be rebuilt from scratch.
GPU — where the model was born
A flexible generalist
Runs almost any operation out of the box.
Large, forgiving memory — data can sit
almost anywhere and still be reached fast.
The original code “just works.”
Analogy
A well-stocked home kitchen. Every tool
is in a drawer, ingredients anywhere on
the counter. Follow any recipe as written.
Powerful and general —
but power-hungry and expensive.
Spyre — IBM’s efficient accelerator
A specialized speedster
Does one thing extremely fast: multiply
matrices. Many ops aren’t built in.
Memory is rigid — data must be laid out
in fixed slots, and moving it has a cost.
Analogy
A championship kitchen built for ONE dish.
Blazing fast — but every other recipe must
be rewritten using only its tools, with
ingredients pre-arranged in exact spots.
Far more efficient —
if you can fit your recipe to it.
Our work: take the GPU recipe and rewrite every step using only Spyre’s tools — same dish, made to run on the faster, greener machine.
